chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who is carried around (in a chair) and a stone is thrown on his behalf (in Hajj). He said, 'Yes, if he is unable (to do it himself).' And this does not contradict these narrations what has been reported:

key_terms.يُرْمَى عَنْهُ: is thrown on his behalf (referring to the stoning ritual or symbolic act)
key_terms.يُطَافُ بِهِ: is carried around / is circumambulated on behalf of

ai.seo_question: Can a sick or elderly person have someone perform Tawaf on their behalf in Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of *Tawaf al-Na'ib* (substitute circumambulation) is clarified, emphasizing that physical incapacity, rather than mere preference, permits another to perform the ritual on one's behalf. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *ease in hardship* (*al-yusr*), ensuring that the obligation of Hajj remains accessible to the elderly, sick, or disabled without imposing undue burden. The text also links this to the ritual of Rami al-Jamarat, indicating that the same principle of substitution applies to throwing stones when the individual cannot do so themselves.
